coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel E2 (block)
record.summary: Phase 1 rental-apartment parcel at 185 Maryland Street (Block 4116 Lot 008), 50,875 sq ft, entitled for about 280 units with 20% below-market-rate, designed by Kennerly Architecture and Planning. Its 2020 appraisal ($5 million against an $11.3 million DDA threshold) and a second below-threshold appraisal in 2021 triggered the down-market delay that has stalled Phase 1; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments make it the first parcel the developer must take down.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell well short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery -- 13m short at the SW corner, 25m short at the SE corner (a growing gap toward the east, consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors). Extended each south vertex independently by its own measured gap (rather than a uniform shift) so the block's south edge now reaches the real sidewalk across its full width, matching Figure 6.4.2's own convention of drawing blocks flush to the street.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Shown at 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2, the same height tier as Parcel E3. NOTE: this differs from the separately-named 'Parcel E2' elsewhere in Pier 70 sourcing (a Kennerly Architecture and Planning-designed, ~280-unit residential building at 70 ft near Slipways Commons) -- that parcel sits in a different part of the site (per D4D Fig. 6.4.2's parcel labeling, the two 'E2' references may refer to distinct parcels, or reflect a labeling inconsistency between D4D figures; flagged as unresolved rather than merged). No construction-start source found for this block.

open_questions: Whether the '350-unit' first market-rate apartment building Brookfield described in July 2026 is E2: E2 is the only Phase 1 rental parcel with an appraisal and a design approval, but no report names it.

Kennerly's own project page (kennerlyarchitecture.com/portfolio/pier-70-e2/) returned HTTP 503 during this pass; search-engine excerpts of it cite 282 homes and 10,000 sq ft of retail, not restated here until read directly.
The date of the Planning Department's vertical design approval for E2 and the June 2021 appraised value are not published in the retrieved documents.

The 'E2' label: the D4D height figure places E2 south of Building 12 at Maryland Street and 22nd Street; the geometry file records a possible labeling inconsistency between figures. Port documents give the address 185 Maryland Street.
